title: Describing Places with Attitude and Relative Clauses

sections.content:
You know relative clauses with *que*, *quien*, *donde* and *cuyo* from B1 Unit 5 (*La casa donde nos reuníamos*, *la amiga cuyo hermano vive en Madrid*). In descriptive writing and *crónicas*, relative clauses let you weave sensory detail and personal attitude into one flowing sentence.

**Non-restrictive relative clauses** (between commas) add an evaluative aside about a place already identified: *La plaza, que los sábados resulta caótica pero entrañable, conserva su encanto.* **Preposition + donde** (*por donde*, *desde donde*, *hacia donde*) traces movement through space: *el callejón por donde entra el olor del café*.

Use **cuyo / cuya / cuyos / cuyas** to link a place to its sights, sounds or features in a compact, literary way: *un mercado cuyos toldos de colores cubren toda la calle*, *un barrio cuyo bullicio se escucha desde la esquina*. Remember that *cuyo* agrees with the noun that follows it and never takes an article (*cuyos los toldos* ✗).

sections.title: Relative clauses for place and atmosphere
rows: *El callejón, que parece caótico a mediodía, tiene un encanto especial.*
*La esquina desde donde se oye el bullicio del mercado.*
*cuyo / cuya / cuyos / cuyas* (agrees with following noun)
*Una plaza cuyos toldos protegen del sol a los vecinos.*
*una calle que sus toldos...* ✗ → *una calle cuyos toldos...* ✓

items.spanish: Cruzamos un callejón pintoresco por donde apenas pasa una persona.
items.english: We crossed a picturesque lane through which barely one person fits.

items.spanish: La plaza, que al amanecer está en silencio, se vuelve ruidosa antes de las nueve.
items.english: The square, which is silent at dawn, becomes noisy before nine.

items.spanish: Entramos en un mercado cuyo bullicio se escucha desde dos esquinas antes.
items.english: We entered a market whose hubbub can be heard from two corners away.

items.spanish: Es un barrio antiguo cuyos toldos de tela dan sombra a los puestos de fruta.
items.english: It is an old neighbourhood whose cloth awnings shade the fruit stalls.

sections.content: In careful Spanish, avoid *que su* (*un barrio que su bullicio...* ✗) and use *cuyo/cuya/cuyos/cuyas* agreeing with the possessed noun (*un barrio cuyo bullicio...*, *una plaza cuyas esquinas...*).
